references_experience.text: ng Assisted Electronic Monitoring of West Coast Fixed Gear Fisheries. The Northwest Fisheries Science Center seeks a vendor to establish and refine Electronic Monitoring protocols for the fixed gear fleet that provide a full accounting of all catch. This requirement seeks to develop and implement comprehensive assessment techniques for quota management and integration into stock assessments. This acquisition is 100% set aside for small business concerns. The associated NAICS code is 541511, Custom Computer Programming Services, and the small business size standard is $34 million. If you would like to submit a quotation, follow the instru ctions in Section L of the solicitation, complete the required portions of the attached document, and submit it to the a ddress shown on the Standard Form that follows this letter. The U.S. Government intends to award an indefinite-quantity indefinite-delivery type of contract to the responsible company submitting an acceptable offer at th e lowest price. We intend to award a contract based on initial proposals, without holding discussions, although we may hold discussions with companies in the competitive range if there is a need to do so. Quotations are due September 11, 2026, at 10:00 hours. No quotations will be accepted after this time. Quotations must be in English and incomplete quotations will not be accepted. Your quotation must be submitted electronically to GuatemalaBids@state.gov. It is important to make sure the submission is made in Adobe Acrobat (pdf) file format. The file size must not exceed 30MB. If the file size should exceed 30MB, the submission must be made in separate files and attached to separate emails with less than 30MB each. For a quotation to be considered, you must also complete and submit the following: 1. SF-1449 2. Section 1, Pricing 3. Section 5 Representations and Certifications 4. This justification authorizes and dictates the acquisition of specific, brand-name industrial automation, network, and scanning hardware—specifically Schweitzer Engineering Laboratories (SEL) network switches, Rockwell Automation/Allen-Bradley control platforms, and Datalogic industrial scanners—necessary to support the deployment, integration, and sustainment of the Defense Logistics Agency (DLA) Material Flow System (MFS). The requirement for these specific manufacturers is based entirely on the technical parameters of the existing solution and the DLA Enterprise Approved Architecture, not on subjective vendor preference. Standardizing on these chosen enterprise brands is operationally necessary to align long-term sustainment, configuration management, and maintenance processes. Utilizing non-standard hardware would introduce disparate system architectures, exponentially increasing lifecycle maintenance costs and degrading operational readiness by disrupting the required interoperability across the physical and digital layers of DLA's critical material-handling infrastructure. Insoweit stehen mehrere Systeme zur Verfügung, die die geforderten Leistungsparameter erfüllen. Gleichzeitig wird gefordert, dass der angebotene Rückkaufpreis dem „vollen Wert“ im Sinne des § 63 Abs. 3 LHO entsprechen muss. Die Anforderung ist unseres Erachtens aus vergaberechtlicher Sicht nicht hinreichend transparent und erschwert eine Angebotserstellung. Da Art und Umfang der zurückzubauenden Anlagenteile sowie die zum Zeitpunkt des Rückbaus geltenden technischen, rechtlichen und wirtschaftlichen Rahmenbedingungen derzeit nicht belastbar vorhersehbar sind, ist eine sachgerechte Kalkulation dieser Leistung über einen derart langen Zeitraum nur unter Berücksichtigung entsprechender Risikozuschläge möglich.
